- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is significantly above recent mean, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low sentiment period, cap the peak at +10% above the 14-day moving average to prevent overshoot.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is below recent mean, add 3–5% to forecast to counteract pessimism.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the first 5 days show consistent upward trend, adjust downward by 2–3% in the 6th–10th day to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (e.g., alternating 0.00 and 0.75), reduce forecast variance by 15–20% to avoid overfitting to noise.
